column1: # Bodo word gold set, written 2026-11-18 from the descriptions below before the Bodo rules were run on
# these items. Format: word, broad pronunciation(s) separated by |, category, source. Sources: K = entry of
# English Wiktionary's "Bodo (India) lemmas" category (CC BY-SA 4.0; spelling, romanisation and gloss read
# 2026-11-18); U = example word of "Representation of Bodo, Dogri and Maithili languages in Unicode
# Standard", Government of India, Unicode document L2/08-197 (2008); N = Bodo numeral as listed in the
# Wikipedia article "Boro language (India)" (CC BY-SA 4.0), in the Devanagari spelling of IndicCorp v2
# Bodo text; C = word of the Bodo locale of Unicode CLDR (common/main/brx.xml, Unicode License v3); I =
# word attested in Bodo text of AI4Bharat IndicCorp v2 (CC0). Pronunciations hand-written with the
# phoneme inventory of Bhattacharya (1977, A Descriptive Analysis of the Boro Language, as given by
# Sarmah 2004 and the Wikipedia article: i e a ɔ u ɯ; pʰ tʰ kʰ b d ɡ m n ŋ s z r l h j w; no voiced
# aspirates, no retroflex or palatal stops) and the spelling conventions of L2/08-197 and of the
# Devanagari and Latin versions of the first article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights:
# ो ॊ = ɯ, ै = ɯi, ौ = ɯu, the inherent vowel = ɔ, an apostrophe after a consonant = its inherent vowel
# said; a bare consonant at the end of a word or before another consonant is said without a vowel (Hindi
# type), except in the first syllable; ं = ŋ; य व after a vowel and before a consonant or the end of the
# word = the second half of a diphthong (i, u); च छ श ष स = s, ज झ = z, ट ठ ड ढ ण = t tʰ d d n, ड़ = r,
# घ ध भ = ɡ d b in loanwords; vowel length is not written. Tone (high or low, on the last syllable of a
# word: Sarmah 2004) is not written in Bodo Devanagari and is left out here; Wiktionary's tones for गं,
# दाव and बिमा are therefore not part of the expected forms. Wiktionary's romanisation writes ɯ with o
# in some entries (लोगो logo, बोराइ borai); the Devanagari ो is read ɯ as the Unicode document gives it.
# Bodo sentence gold set, written 2026-11-18 before the Bodo rules were run on these items. The first
# sentence is the first article of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Bodo Devanagari as quoted
# in the Wikipedia article "Boro language (India)" (CC BY-SA 4.0), with the pronunciation taken from the
# Latin version quoted there ("Gaswi subung anw udangwi man sanman arw mwnthai lana jwnwm layw"); the
# others are lines of AI4Bharat IndicCorp v2 Bodo text (CC0) that are in none of tools/eval/data/brx_dev.tsv,
# brx_heldout.tsv and brx_flores.tsv. Pronunciation hand-written with the conventions of words.src.
